chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id, from Ibn Abi 'Umayr and 'Ali ibn Hadid, from Jamil, from some of his companions, from one of the two of them عليهما السلام, that he said:
Regarding the tooth of a boy: a man strikes it, so it falls out, then it grows again. He said: “There is no qisas upon him, but the arsh is upon him.”

key_terms.الْأَرْشُ: monetary compensation assessed for bodily injury
key_terms.تَسْقُطُ: falls out as a result of the blow
key_terms.سِنِّ: tooth, specifically the injured tooth under discussion

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling if someone knocks out a child's tooth and it grows back?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling concerning injury to the tooth of a child when the tooth falls out and then grows again. In that case, qisas does not apply, but financial compensation ('arsh) is still due for the injury.
